places.name: {block} Mill Hall
places.blurb: The free Mill table three times a day, at long tables under felt. The robots cook to the standard recipe and the regulars correct it at the table with vinegar, chili and several decades of argument.
dishes: Lamp-dawn jook with chili crisp and sour-starch puffs
Cold glass noodles and jelly cubes in black vinegar
A bowl of the Nine on every table
places.tip: Come at lamp-dawn, before the night crews finish the chili crisp.

places.name: The Long Table
places.blurb: Four hundred seats at one table, a paid cook and a crew of volunteers who mostly came for the talk. Strangers are seated together on purpose. If you get on too well, an aunt moves you along.
dishes: Pressure-cooker curry over Mill rice, glossed with cultivated pork fat
Whatever the aunts made: one family dish from each volunteer
Mill lager, poured from the end of the table
places.tip: Offer to carry the pots back: it is the quickest way to be told the family recipes.

places.name: The Quiet Hall
places.where: the {block} hall, at the edge of the wood
places.blurb: Nobody talks at supper here, so you hear the spoons, the lids and the drum's fans. The cook chalks the menu on a slate by the door and rubs each line out as its pot empties.
dishes: Jook of Mill jasmine rice with herbs from the pot
Mycelium broth, held below a simmer since morning
Steamed starch cake with black sugar
places.tip: Borrow a slate at the door; writing thanks to the cook on it counts as a speech here.

places.name: Aunts' Kitchen
places.blurb: A small hall where each volunteer cooks one dish from their own table and the paid cook makes rice for everyone. A different supper every night, and the same aunts.
dishes: Rice from the hall's big cooker, sticky and jasmine-scented
An aunt's dish: braised curd in black vinegar, or whatever came
One tomato, cut eight ways for the table
Mill lager
places.tip: Ask whose dish is whose, and every aunt will tell you, starting with their grandmother.

places.name: Felt Hall
places.blurb: Named for its ceiling, which three generations of the block have felted, mended and argued over. You can hear the person opposite without leaning in, which in a hall this size is a luxury.
dishes: Red palm-style stew with fried jelly cubes and a starch swallow
Sourdough heel with cultured butter
Crème caramel, lidded
places.tip: Look up as you sit: the newest patch is over the pass, and whoever sewed it is probably serving.

places.name: Ring {ring} Hall
places.where: Station Ring {ring}, one deck above the Quaysides
places.blurb: The hall that feeds the freight crews, the Gate staff and whoever has just glided in. The tables face the Ledger, so supper comes with the year's births and deaths scrolling past.
dishes: Noodles in a peppery Mill broth, the ring counter's big sister
Mycelium skewers off the induction rail, salted
Pint of Mill lager
places.tip: When a crew is called to a train they leave mid-bowl, and the pickles are then anyone's.

places.name: The Rota
places.blurb: Each night a different household from the block cooks, under a rota older than anyone on it. Some nights are famous and some are rice and apologies. The board by the door says whose turn it is.
dishes: The house dish of whoever's turn it is
Sticky rice with chili crisp
Lactic sour from the block's crock
places.tip: Check the board before you come, as locals plan their week round three names on it.

places.name: The Second Sitting
places.where: the Keel, beside the Ring {ring} lifts
places.blurb: The free Mill table in the lamp-night, for the people who run the laundries, the Yards and the batch work. The jook has sat on the loop since dusk and is softer for it. Warm, quiet and full of yawning.
dishes: Midnight jook, held on the loop since dusk
Fried jelly cubes in sweet-savoury broth
Milk tea with Mill creamer
places.tip: Come after one, when the laundry shift arrives with pickles.

places.name: Pot and Choir
places.blurb: A cooked hall whose volunteers are also its choir, so the soup comes round between verses. The ceiling is felted in three colours and the room still rings. Some wanderers route a whole year through here.
dishes: Hot pot for six, lidded: curds, glass noodles and greens
Steamed buns with mycelium and black sugar
Mill lager by the jug
places.tip: Hum if you know it, and clap at the end of the meal, never the end of a song.

places.name: The Children's Hall
places.blurb: The school hall at noon, where the oldest class serves the youngest and any visitor who asks. Portions are measured by children, so they vary. The jelly cubes are cut to the width of a ruler.
dishes: Cold glass noodles in chili oil, mild on request
Starch jelly cubes, cut by the oldest class
Amazake in a lidded cup
places.tip: Thank your server by name: there is a chart on the wall and it matters a great deal.

places.name: Elders' Hall
places.blurb: A hall on the high decks where the food is soft, the lamps are good and the talk is long. The cooks are in their eighties and cook as they always have. A guest under thirty gets fussed over.
dishes: Mycelium braised in koji tare until it falls apart
Custard set on the loop, with black sugar
Jasmine tea, refilled without asking
places.tip: Bring herbs, since each sprig earns a story and probably a second custard.

places.name: The Shift Hall
places.where: the Keel, between the Mill and the vat halls
places.blurb: The food plant's own canteen, where the Mill crews eat what came off the line that morning. On a good day it is the freshest food in the drum, made a hundred metres from your bowl.
dishes: Noodles extruded an hour ago, in glycine-alanine broth
Sour-starch puffs from the test oven
Mill lager from the brewing line's test tank
places.tip: Ask the crews what failed spec today; off-spec sugar glass is the best thing in the room.

places.name: The Wide Lid
places.blurb: One pot the width of a table sits in the middle of the room, under a lid that takes two people to lift. Everyone ladles from it. Heliox would have it cold in minutes, so the lid goes back between turns.
dishes: The big pot: red stew with curds, glass noodles and swallow
Pickled cucumber, two thin slices
Lactic sour
places.tip: Wait for the lid, because lifting it out of turn earns a look from the whole room.

places.name: Court Supper
places.where: the {block} Court, after the block court
places.blurb: Once a week the block meets in its atrium to settle the rota and the light, then eats. Supper is the free table plus whatever people carried down from their flats. Votes have been won on the pickles.
dishes: Night stew with a starch swallow, from the commons
Jars from the flats: pickles, chili crisp, someone's aged cheese
Mill lager
places.tip: Sit through the vote: supper starts the moment the light question is settled, and not before.

places.name: The Guest Pot
places.where: the wanderers' hall by Station Ring {ring}
places.blurb: Wanderers add a spoon of something from their last drum to the hall's stockpot, and the cook tastes each one and decides whether it stays. Most of it does. The broth tastes of half the raft and changes nightly.
dishes: A bowl of the guest pot, over glass noodles
Sticky rice ball with a seam of chili crisp
Amazake, warm from the loop
places.tip: Add something small and say where it came from; the cook keeps a book.

places.name: Dish and Story
places.blurb: A cooked hall with a teaching kitchen at one end: a class of twenty makes supper for two hundred, under one patient cook. Results vary. The dumplings are honest about who folded them.
dishes: Crystal dumplings folded by the class, some of them handsome
Mycelium braised in miso, taught slowly
Cendol-style jelly in coconut-style cream
places.tip: Ask to join the class: guests may fold, and nobody inspects the pleats until the end.

places.name: Ring {ring} Hatch
places.where: Station Ring {ring}, at the platform end
places.blurb: The ring counter: a cup of Mill broth and a sticky rice ball, free, for crews, commuters and anyone off a glide. This one's broth is black-peppery and a little sour, and the regulars defend it with feeling.
dishes: A cup of the house broth, peppery and sour
Sticky rice ball
places.tip: Drink it on the platform, because glide cars do not take hot soup and the crews will tell you why.

places.name: The Quay Fryer
places.blurb: A hatch with one fryer and a queue of freight crews: sour-starch puffs, krupuk and jelly cubes, salted while they still crackle. Frying draws power, so they fry in batches and you wait for yours.
dishes: Sour-starch cheese-bread puffs, a paper cone of six
Krupuk with chili crisp
Fried jelly cubes in salt and black vinegar
places.tip: Wait for the next batch, as the puffs on the rack have already gone quiet.

places.name: Gate Side
places.blurb: A stall for people waiting while the Gate sequences their starters and crocks. Clearance takes an hour if you are lucky, so the bowls are deep and nobody hurries you off the stools.
dishes: Noodles in broth, the slow kind, for slow clearances
Tea in a lidded cup, refilled while you wait
Black sugar mochi, two to a paper
places.tip: Sit where you can see the clearance board, and keep your lid on while you wait.

places.name: Catch Cups
places.blurb: A hatch at the end of the catch cradle, selling hot drinks to people who have just had a full g come back over two seconds. Sweet, warm and steadying. Some elders say it is the only reason they glide.
dishes: Warm amazake, sweetened for shaky legs
Ginger milk tea
A sugar biscuit stamped with the ring number
places.tip: Sit on the bench a moment before you stand; the counter is ten paces away and will wait.

places.name: The Dumpling Window
places.where: the Quaysides, behind the freight scales
places.blurb: Crystal dumplings by the half-dozen, steamed in lidded baskets and handed over still lidded. The wrappers are Mill starch; the filling is mycelium and garden chive, which explains the queue.
dishes: Six crystal dumplings, mycelium and garden chive
Black vinegar and chili oil to dip
Jasmine tea
places.tip: Keep the basket lidded until you sit, or the dumplings cool before you find a bench.

places.name: The Bun Hatch
places.where: the lift lobby on deck {deck}, by {street}
places.blurb: Steamed buns at the lift doors, for people with a cab to catch. The dough is gluten and Mill starch, proved overnight on the waste-heat loop. The black sugar bun leaks if you are not careful.
dishes: Steamed bun with pulled mycelium in hoisin-style glaze
Black sugar bun
Warm soy-style milk
places.tip: Eat the black sugar bun leaning forward, because a mended collar shows syrup.

places.name: Crepe Corner
places.where: where {street} meets the lift core, deck {deck}
places.blurb: Tapioca crepes off an induction plate, folded round whatever is in the tins: coconut-style cream and black sugar, or blight cheese and chili. The plate is the only hot thing on the stall, and the cook guards it.
dishes: Tapioca crepe with coconut-style cream and black sugar
Tapioca crepe with blight cheese and chili crisp
Lactic soda
places.tip: Order two and eat the first standing, since the second comes off a properly hot plate.

places.name: Late Lift Counter
places.where: the lift core at the end of {street}
places.blurb: Jook to go, in lidded cups with a felt sleeve, for people coming off the lamp-night shift. The cups come back washed or they do not come back. The counter keeps a tally and says nothing.
dishes: Jook in a lidded cup with the Nine and spring onion
Two sour-starch puffs
Milk tea
places.tip: Return your cup, because the counter knows whose it was and remembers for years.

places.name: The Toastie Hatch
places.blurb: Cheese toasties pressed on an induction plate until the edges lace. Eat yours on the platform: crumbs float for the whole glide, and the next riders will know exactly what you had.
dishes: Cheese toastie on sourdough, edges laced
Toastie with black garlic and chili
A slice of pickled cucumber
places.tip: Finish it before your car is called, as nobody wants your crumbs at zero g.

places.name: Skewer Rail
places.where: the Quaysides, under the departures board
places.blurb: Mycelium and protein-flour skewers seared on an induction rail one row at a time, because searing draws power and the stall pays for it. Salt, koji glaze or chili, and a cup of broth to stand them in.
dishes: Three mycelium skewers in koji glaze
Protein-flour skewer brushed with cultivated chicken fat
A cup of broth to stand them in
places.tip: Ask for the end of the rail, where the skewers get a second pass and the glaze catches.

places.name: The Lidded Tin
places.where: Station Ring {ring}, by the cycler capsule lifts
places.blurb: A counter for people catching a slow cycler, selling food that behaves without weight: soup in bulbs, bread in nets, dumplings in string bags. The staff have watched a great many people learn this the hard way.
dishes: Soup in a bulb with a straw
Four bread rolls in a net
Dumplings in a string bag
places.tip: Buy the net of rolls, since anything that crumbs becomes a cloud by your first evening aboard.

places.name: Platform Pie
places.blurb: Hand pies in a lard-style crust, filled with curried mycelium or black sugar custard. Pastry is the cheapest thing in the drum and the stall knows it: the crust is generous and the filling is a rumour.
dishes: Curried mycelium hand pie
Black sugar custard hand pie
Lactic sour
places.tip: Take the custard pie warm from the loop shelf; the cold ones are for crews who forgot.

places.name: Loop Kitchen
places.where: the Keel, beside the vat halls' heat exchangers
places.blurb: Everything here cooks on the 65 °C loop, slowly and for nothing, and the board is written by the clock: what has held since lamp-dawn, since yesterday, since last week. Only the bread is toasted.
dishes: Mycelium held at 60 °C overnight, sliced thick, with miso butter
Onsen custard with koji tare
Amazake, brewed since yesterday
Sourdough toast, the one hot thing
places.tip: Order whatever has held longest; the board counts it in hours and regulars go by the biggest number.

places.name: The Slow Pot
places.blurb: A master stock held below a simmer on the loop for two hundred and eleven years, topped up daily and never boiled. Curds, mycelium and noodles are poached in it to order. It darkens a little every decade.
dishes: Mycelium poached in the master stock, sliced, with spring onion
Curds poached in the stock, glassy with fat
A cup of the stock, to drink
Rice to soak up the rest
places.tip: Ask to see the stock ledger: every top-up since the founding, by date and by cook.

places.name: Amazake House
places.blurb: Sweet rice drinks brewed overnight at 60 °C, where koji works best and the loop costs nothing. Plain, ginger, black sugar or sour. Nothing here is boiled, and the owners regard a kettle as a small failure.
dishes: Warm amazake, plain
Amazake with black sugar and a pinch of salt
Rice cake toasted on the plate
places.tip: Try the sour one last: amazake left another day with a lactic culture, and the best thing on the board.

places.name: Five Weeks
places.where: {street}, three doors from the lift core
places.blurb: Named for how long the garlic sits on the loop before it turns soft, black and sweet. Garlic is a Garden crop bought by the head, so it is the dearest thing on plates that cost almost nothing to cook.
dishes: Black garlic toast on sourdough with cultured butter
Mycelium steak with black garlic jus
Black garlic ice cream, non-dairy
places.tip: Buy a head to take home; it comes wrapped in paper and keeps for months on a larder shelf.

places.name: The Hot Room
places.where: the Keel, in the old pipe gallery
places.blurb: A canteen in the gallery where the loop's pipes run, warm enough that soup would stay hot without a lid. Everyone uses a lid anyway. Plant workers come in pink and leave pinker.
dishes: Broth held below a simmer since the morning shift
Glass noodles and curds to drop in
Steamed bun, proved on the pipes
Amazake
places.tip: Hang your coat by the door, since steam in a lining takes a day to dry.

places.name: Sixty-Three
places.blurb: Named for the temperature at which everything here sets, where vat egg barely holds and custard trembles. Four custards, savoury to sweet, then one hot thing seared on the plate in front of you.
dishes: Onsen custard with koji tare and spring onion
Steamed-style custard with mycelium and garden chive, set on the loop
Black sugar custard, barely set
The hot thing: a seared curd, salted
places.tip: Eat them in the order they come, as the cooks have timed the sequence to the minute.

places.name: Held
places.blurb: Twelve courses, each held on the loop at its own temperature for its own time, from a custard set at 61 °C for an hour to cultivated beef held at 58 °C for three days. The cooks own more thermometers than knives. Nothing boils.
dishes: Vat egg custard, 61 °C for an hour, with garden chive
Cultivated beef held at 58 °C for three days, one thick slice
Black garlic and a single seared shiitake
Amazake sorbet over warm koji cream
places.tip: Book three days ahead, because the beef for your sitting goes on the loop the day you book.

places.name: Overnight
places.blurb: A commons breakfast room where everything went on the loop the night before: jook held until it turns to silk, sweet starch porridge, amazake. Keeping it warm costs the drum nothing, so it opens whenever you wake.
dishes: Overnight jook, silk-smooth, with chili crisp and the Nine
Sweet starch porridge with black sugar
Amazake
places.tip: Come before seven, when the jook has held nine hours and the regulars say it peaks.

places.name: Below a Simmer
places.blurb: Clear broths only, held under a simmer for a day so nothing clouds. Five on the board at once, from glycine-sweet to sour and peppery, with noodles or rice to drop into any of them. People come here to taste, not talk.
dishes: A flight of clear broths, three small cups
Glass noodles or rice to add
Curds poached in the broth of your choice
places.tip: Start with the palest broth and work darker, the way the cooks taste each morning.

places.name: The Hot Bench
places.where: the Quaysides, by the freight lifts
places.blurb: Mycelium confit, held in fat at 65 °C for twelve hours until it pulls apart, piled on rice for crews coming off shift. The bench along the wall is warmed by the pipe underneath, and nobody leaves it quickly.
dishes: Mycelium confit on rice, with pickles
A ladle of the confit fat over your rice
Lactic sour
places.tip: Ask for the crisped end; they sear one batch an hour for it and there is never enough.

places.name: The Incubator
places.where: the Keel, in the strain library's old incubation room
places.blurb: A café in a room built to keep cultures warm, which it still does: yoghurt set overnight, tempeh-style cakes grown on the shelves, and a miso that has been in the corner longer than the café.
dishes: Yoghurt set overnight, with berry purée
Tempeh-style cake, sliced and seared
Miso soup from the corner crock
places.tip: Sit against the spinward wall, which backs onto the incubators and is the warmest seat in the Keel.

places.name: Bath and Bowl
places.blurb: A long soak in loop-heated water, a lidded bowl in a robe, then a nap on a warm bench, sold as one ticket. The bath is the cheapest part. The bowl changes daily and is held on the same pipes as the water.
dishes: The day's bowl: noodles in a broth that never boiled
Onsen custard on the side
A cold lactic soda after the heat
places.tip: Take the nap: the bench runs off the same loop and the ticket includes it.

places.name: Third Terrace
places.where: the Hollow's back end wall, the third-g terrace
places.blurb: A terrace at a third of a g, with the far bank of the Hollow hanging overhead as the sunline dims to dusk. Soufflés stand a hand higher here and fall slower, and the kitchen builds the whole menu round that.
dishes: Third-g soufflé on precision casein, still standing at the table
Mycelium steak, seared, with béarnaise
A cherry tomato for each guest, warm from the lamp
Pulled sugar that hangs in long threads
places.tip: Book the dusk sitting, when the sunline dims overhead and the soufflé arrives with the lamps.

places.name: The Tall Soufflé
places.where: the front end wall, fourth tier, a third of a g
places.blurb: One dish in nine flavours: a soufflé baked at a third of a g, where a foam weighs a third of what it does on the low decks. It rises a hand higher than it would down there and takes its time falling.
dishes: Cheese soufflé on precision casein
Black sugar soufflé with cold custard poured in
Lamp-grown cress, the only crunch
Coffee
places.tip: Order the second soufflé when the first arrives, since the oven takes exactly as long as you will.

places.name: Night Netting
places.where: the Spindle in the lamp-night, by the back flying hall
places.blurb: When the Spindle opens at lamp-night, a crew strings a net between two anchor lines and serves supper inside it to people in wing-sleeves. Everything comes in bulbs, bags or skins, and the crumbs are swept up with a fan.
dishes: Broth in a bulb, sent up hot from the lift lobby
Six dumplings in a string bag
Mochi, which does not crumb
places.tip: Clip your sleeve to the net before you eat; one sneeze and you are drifting across the axis with your soup.

places.name: The Bend
places.where: the back end wall, the quarter-g terrace bar
places.blurb: A terrace bar where drinks are poured from two metres up and the stream bends a hand's width off its aim on the way down. The pourers allow for it. Newcomers hold their glass under the bottle and get wet.
dishes: Long-poured gin and lactic soda
Long-poured jasmine tea, for the sober
Krupuk and chili crisp
Sugar-glass shards over cold jelly
places.tip: Let the pourer place your glass; the right spot depends on which way the bar faces, and only the staff remember.

places.name: Top Tier Kiosk
places.where: the top garden terrace of the front end wall
places.blurb: A kiosk on the highest terrace, where a child can jump the height of a house and the adults pretend not to try. Lidded picnic boxes to eat on the grass, with the Hollow curving away on every side.
dishes: Picnic box: rice balls, pickles, a wedge of cheese, a pastry
One strawberry, in the box's corner
Lactic soda in a stoppered bottle
places.tip: Keep a hand on the box lid; up here a knock sends it drifting slowly down onto the next terrace.

places.name: Featherweight
places.where: the back end wall, the tenth-g terrace
places.blurb: A pastry kitchen at a tenth of a g, where meringue stands as tall as the cook can pipe it and laminated dough rises without crushing its own layers. The pastry is cheap; the hours of the two cooks are not.
dishes: Meringue tower, piped a hand and a half high
Hundred-layer pastry that never settled
Soufflé omelette on vat egg
Coffee poured from height
places.tip: Do not take a tower home: it slumps a little on every deck the cab drops.

places.name: Flying Hall Canteen
places.where: the front flying hall, below the sleeve racks
places.blurb: The free table at the foot of the flying hall, for people coming down from the netting with sore shoulders. The jook is made thick enough to stay on a spoon this near the axis.
dishes: Thick jook with the Nine and chili crisp
Rice balls in string bags, for the climb back
Amazake in a lidded bulb
places.tip: Take the lowest tables, where your weight has come back enough for soup to behave like soup.

places.name: Leap Supper
places.where: the dance terrace on the back end wall, a third of a g
places.blurb: Supper between sets on the low-g dance terrace, where the reels leap and every landing comes down a hand's width spinward. Bowls have weighted bases, because a dancer landing near your table moves the air.
dishes: Curry noodles with cultivated chicken fat, in a weighted bowl
Starch jelly in black syrup
Mill lager in a lidded mug
places.tip: Sit antispinward of the floor, where every leap drifts away from your table rather than into it.

places.name: The Upside Table
places.where: the end wall's sixth tier, a fifth of a g
places.blurb: From this terrace the Hollow is a tube of lawns, lake and woods running away on every side, with picnickers upside down overhead. The food is plain and good. Nobody comes for the food.
dishes: Mycelium skewers with a koji glaze
Cucumber, cold and salted
Sourdough with cultured butter
Gin and lactic soda
places.tip: Ask for a seat facing along the axis, where the lake hangs straight overhead.

places.name: The Upper Tier
places.where: the highest kitchen on the back end wall, a sixth of a g
places.blurb: Ten courses cooked where a sixth of a g lets sugar pull into threads a metre long and soufflés stand as tall as their dishes are wide. Ten cooks, thirty seats, booked months ahead. Guests are shown the kitchen and asked to jump.
dishes: Spun sugar pulled a metre long at the pass
Sixth-g cheese soufflé, as tall as its dish is wide
Cultivated steak, 120 g, basted in cultured butter
Half an orchard pear, cut at the table
places.tip: Say yes when they ask you to jump in the kitchen; the cooks count it as a course.

places.name: The Crock Wall
places.blurb: A bakery with a wall of three hundred labelled crocks: the block's own starters, fed here overnight on the loop for a small fee while their families sleep. The house loaf comes from whichever crock the baker likes best that week.
dishes: The week's loaf, from a neighbour's starter
Sourdough heel with cultured butter and salt
Coffee
places.tip: Ask whose crock made this week's loaf, and expect its family history at length.

places.name: Spoon and Crumb
places.where: Station Ring {ring}, at the top of the platform lifts
places.blurb: A station bakery with a shelf of starter crocks for wanderers: take a spoon, leave a spoon. The bread changes as the shelf does. In a good year the house loaf has a little of forty drums in it.
dishes: The shelf loaf, never the same twice
Croissant laminated with cultured butter
Milk tea
places.tip: Bring a spoon of starter from your last drum and the baker will trade you a heel of today's loaf.

places.name: Lamp-Dawn Bakery
places.blurb: Opens at five, before the lamps come up, on the drum's cheapest power. The croissants come out as the street lamps ramp up at half past six. By seven the shelf is crumbs and apologies.
dishes: Croissant laminated with cultured butter
Black sugar knot
Coffee
places.tip: Come at twenty past six, before the lamps ramp up and the queue wakes.

places.name: The Starch Oven
places.where: the {block} arcade, by the Mill Hall
places.blurb: Mill-only baking: starch-and-fibre loaves, sour-starch cheese puffs and tapioca flatbreads, with no gluten in the building. The cheapest bakery in the drum, and the one people with long memories of blights trust.
dishes: Sour-starch cheese puffs, a bag of ten
Soft starch loaf, sliced
Tapioca flatbread with chili crisp
places.tip: Eat the puffs on the spot, since by the next deck they have gone from crisp to chewy.

places.name: The Pie Shelf
places.blurb: Pies in lard-style crusts, stacked under lids on a heated shelf. Pastry is cheap and the shelf is long. The savoury pies hold curried mycelium, the sweet ones berry purée, and in both the crust is the point.
dishes: Mycelium and gravy pie
Berry pie with a lattice top
A jug of custard to share
places.tip: Ask for the end pie, which sits nearest the element and has the darkest bottom crust in the drum.

places.name: Laminate
places.blurb: Croissants laminated by hand to eighty-one layers of cultured butter, and nothing on the counter that is not laminated. Butter is the dear line, so every pastry is weighed. People cross the raft for them and say they were passing.
dishes: The croissant, eighty-one layers
Kouign-amann with black sugar
Laminated cheese twist
Coffee
places.tip: Come at nine for the second bake, as the first goes to high-deck elders who queue in silence and buy dozens.

places.name: Night Bakery
places.blurb: Bakes through the lamp-night, when power is cheapest, and sells from a hatch to laundry crews and insomniacs. The bread is plain and very good. The baker talks to anyone awake.
dishes: Hot roll, split and buttered
Bun with chili crisp baked in
Milk tea
places.tip: Knock twice at the hatch after two; the baker naps between batches and wakes for regulars.

places.name: The Steamer
places.blurb: A bakery with no oven, only steamers: yeast-raised rice cakes with a honeycomb crumb, buns, and sweet starch cakes in paper cases. Steam is cheap when the water already starts at 65 °C.
dishes: Yeast-raised steamed rice cake, still warm
Steamed bun with sweet curd filling
Pandan-style starch cake
places.tip: Buy the rice cake warm; cold, it is merely good.

places.name: The Flatbread Hatch
places.where: the {block} night market, at the end of {street}
places.blurb: Flatbreads slapped onto an induction plate and blistered in under a minute, then folded round whatever the tins hold. The plate draws power, so the cook keeps it full.
dishes: Flatbread with chili crisp and garden chive
Flatbread folded round blight cheese
Lactic soda
places.tip: Join the queue when it is long, because a full plate is a hot plate.

places.name: Crumb Court
places.blurb: A bakery in the corner of the atrium, under terraces of herb shelves. Pastry is the staple here and nobody apologises for it: four croissants, two tarts, and a cucumber sandwich on Fridays that sells out in minutes.
dishes: Croissant with a sesame-style crust
Custard tart, set on the loop
Friday cucumber sandwich, crusts off
places.tip: Be there at ten on Friday; the cucumber sandwiches are counted out one a head.

places.name: The Rusk House
places.where: the Keel, beside the survival reserve stores
places.blurb: Hard breads for larders: rusks, crispbread and hard rings that keep for years. Most of the trade is households restocking after Knotnight. The café corner sells yesterday's rusks dunked in today's tea.
dishes: Rusks dunked in milk tea
Crispbread with aged cheese
A larder ring, hard enough to need the tea
places.tip: A bag of rusks is a host gift that says you thought about their larder.

places.name: The Proving Shelf
places.where: the Keel, beside the loop's main return
places.blurb: A bakery that proves its dough on shelves above the loop's return pipe, which keeps a steady 30 °C day and night for nothing. The baker says the bread can tell. The cinnamon knots are better than they need to be.
dishes: Cinnamon knot, glazed
Country loaf, by the half
Coffee
places.tip: Buy the knots before noon, when the shelves fill with tomorrow's dough and the seats go with them.

places.name: Across the Grain
places.blurb: A mycelium steakhouse that slices across the fibre, the way butchers once did, and sears each steak on induction while you watch. Basted in butter and cultivated beef fat, it reads as beef to everyone, none of whom has had beef.
dishes: Mycelium steak, seared, basted with cultivated beef fat
Frites and béarnaise with garden tarragon
A glass of red from plant-cell grapes
places.tip: Ask for it cut thin across the fibre; the thick cut is for people who like to chew while they talk.

places.name: The Cheese Room
places.where: the Keel, in the cool room beside the precision vats
places.blurb: Cheeses aged in the coolest room in the Keel, on shelves that have held cheese for nine centuries. Precision casein, Mill butterfat and old cultures, and a cheesemonger who knows which blight each line survived.
dishes: A board of four cheeses, each with its vintage
Crackers and black sugar paste
A glass of lactic sour
places.tip: Say what you taste in each cheese before the monger tells you; guesses are kept in a book.

places.name: Shio
places.blurb: Eight seats round a koji room you can see through glass. Everything is marinated in shio-koji, aged on koji or fermented with it, down to the dessert. The cook keeps four strains and talks about them like grandchildren.
dishes: Mycelium cured three days in shio-koji, seared once
Koji-aged cultivated pork fat over hot rice
Miso caramel over non-dairy ice cream
Warm sake, Mill starch and koji
places.tip: Take the corner seat by the glass, where the koji room's warmth comes through.

places.name: The Curd
places.blurb: Tofu-style curds pressed from protein flour every morning and sold warm: fried, braised, or silken in syrup. Protein flour is cheap, so the only dear thing here is the presser's early start.
dishes: Warm silken curd in black syrup
Mapo-style curd with chili and sanshool
Fried curd skins, salted
Rice
places.tip: Order the mapo medium, because hot here is calibrated for regulars who stopped feeling sanshool years ago.

places.name: Set
places.blurb: A dairy bar of things that set: panna cotta on precision gelatin, crème caramel, yoghurt custard, junket. Each wobbles at its own rate, and the counter staff can tell them apart by the tremble.
dishes: Panna cotta that melts at mouth temperature
Crème caramel, lidded
Yoghurt with berry purée
places.tip: Tap the counter gently when the tray arrives and the staff will name each dessert by its shiver.

places.name: The Burger Line
places.blurb: Hybrid burgers: mycelium for the chew, cultivated beef fat for the taste of an animal nobody here has met. Seared on induction eight at a time and lidded the second they leave the plate.
dishes: Hybrid burger with aged cheese and pickles
Frites with a pot of mayonnaise
Lactic cola
places.tip: Eat it at the counter with the lid close by, as heliox sets the cheese within a minute.

places.name: The Hanging Room
places.where: the Keel, behind the strain library
places.blurb: Koji-aged mycelium charcuterie, hung in a room kept as damp as a good cellar. Ham cut as thin as paper, bacon cured with smoke-style phenols, a salami that took nine months. Sliced to order onto a cold board.
dishes: The board: ham, salami and pressed bacon, cut thin
Pickled garden shallots
Sourdough and cultured butter
places.tip: Ask to see the hanging room; the cutter takes guests in once the door has been shut long enough.

places.name: Cake and Culture
places.where: the {block} night market, under the arcade
places.blurb: Tempeh-style cakes grown on Mill starch in trays on the loop shelves, then sliced and fried in a sweet-hot glaze. Cheap, filling and nutty without a nut in the building.
dishes: Fried tempeh-style cake in sweet chili glaze
Rice with pickles
Lactic sour
places.tip: Ask for it extra crisp; they fry those one tray at a time and the cook likes being asked.

places.name: Pull
places.blurb: Personal pizzas on gluten dough with precision casein that melts and stretches the way the old pictures promise. The oven draws power and the cook keeps it full. A fresh tomato on top is extra, and nobody begrudges it.
dishes: Personal pizza with casein cheese and tomato purée
Fresh tomato on top, sliced
Lactic soda
places.tip: Share the fresh tomato across the table; ordering one for yourself is noticed.

places.name: Rendered
places.blurb: The same mycelium five ways, each basted in a different cultivated fat: pork, beef, chicken, duck-style and lamb-style. A lesson in how much of an animal lives in its fat, and the menu says as much.
dishes: Five slices of mycelium, five cultivated fats
Rice cooked in the drippings
A glass of red
Sour pickles, to reset
places.tip: Taste them blind first, as the cook suggests: most people place the chicken and nobody places the lamb.

places.name: Miso House
places.blurb: A room of miso crocks, some older than the street, and a menu of things that go with miso, which is everything. The soup is ladled from a pot held on the loop all day. The crocks sell by the spoon.
dishes: Miso soup with curds and spring onion
Miso-glazed mycelium, seared
Rice with miso butter
places.tip: Buy a spoon of the oldest crock for your larder; it travels well in waxed paper.

places.name: The Yoghurt Window
places.blurb: A hatch selling yoghurt by the cup to children after school and aunts before work. Three cultures, each registered with the strain library, each with its own sourness. The berry purée is plant-cell and the children do not care.
dishes: Yoghurt with berry purée
Drinking yoghurt, salted
Yoghurt with black sugar crunch
places.tip: Ask politely for a taste of all three cultures, which the window gives to anyone who does.

places.name: The Rack Room
places.where: the Keel, among the Garden racks
places.blurb: Six tables between the Garden's LED racks, under light pink enough to make everyone look feverish. Every plate has something cut within the hour, and the menu says how many lamp-hours grew it.
dishes: Salad cut this hour: leaves, cress and pea shoots
Cucumber, cold and salted, cut thick
Tomato with cultured butter and salt
Strawberries with cold custard
places.tip: Ask the grower to cut your herbs at the table; it costs nothing more and the smell is half the meal.

places.name: The Allotment Table
places.blurb: The block keeps a strip of Hollow floor in its rotation, and on its day it cooks what is ripe at a trestle between the rows. The light is free; the ground is not, so everything is grown close and eaten closer.
dishes: Whatever is ripe, raw, with salt and cultured butter
Pea shoots wilted into noodles
Herb-pot pesto on sourdough
places.tip: Help pick before supper and you get the first radish, which is both the custom and the best one.

places.name: The Glass Case
places.blurb: Four tables behind a greengrocer's, where tomatoes from the glass case out front are cut and served on warm sourdough. Each is weighed and named for its rack. The case is lit like a jeweller's window and priced like one.
dishes: A whole tomato, sliced, on warm sourdough with oil
Three cherry tomatoes, warm from the lamp
Pickled green tomato, a sliver
places.tip: Let the grocer choose your tomato, since asking for the biggest marks you as a visitor.

places.name: Pea Shoot
places.where: the {block} arcade, by the lift core
places.blurb: The cheapest crunch in the drum: pea shoots, microgreens and cress, grown a week under lamps and cut by the handful. A week of light costs far less than a month of it, so a bowl of green comes in under half a kWh.
dishes: Bowl of pea shoots in sesame-style dressing
Microgreens over cold glass noodles
Cress sandwich on Mill bread
places.tip: Order the shoots at lamp-dawn, when the morning cut arrives and they still squeak.

places.name: The Green Table
places.where: deck {hdeck}, at the bright end of {street}
places.blurb: Dinner where the dear course is the salad: leaves, cucumber, a tomato and herbs from the drum's own racks, dressed at the table and eaten slowly. The pastry course after is a palate cleanser, priced like one.
dishes: The salad: leaves, cucumber and tomato, dressed at the table
Mycelium steak with herb butter
Pastry course: a croissant cut in four
Garden mint tea
places.tip: Eat the salad slowly; the regulars make it last twenty minutes and the staff notice who rushes.

places.name: Cucumber Club
places.where: the Hollow's edge, near the lake lifts
places.blurb: A members' room whose fee is one cucumber a week, which the club cuts and shares among whoever turns up. Cold, thick and salted, with gin. It has argued about the right thickness for longer than its minutes go back.
dishes: Cucumber, cold, cut thick, salted
Gin with a slice of cucumber
Cucumber sandwiches on Mill bread
places.tip: Ask for the thick cut, because asking for thin starts a discussion that runs past closing.

places.name: The Herb Shelf
places.blurb: A small kitchen that cooks the free table's dishes and covers them in herbs, which cost almost nothing by the gram: basil, shiso, coriander, dill and chive by the fistful. The cheapest way in the drum to eat something green.
dishes: Glass noodles under a fistful of herbs
Jook with shiso and coriander
Herb omelette on vat egg
places.tip: Bring a sprig from your host's shelf and the cook will put it in your bowl.

places.name: Chili House
places.where: the {block} night market, at the end of {street}
places.blurb: Fresh chilies from the racks, rare enough that the menu gives each its rack number and its heat. Everything else is Mill food built to carry them. Fresh chili tastes nothing like capsaicin from the flavourist's shelf, which is the point.
dishes: Fresh green chili sliced over curds and rice
Blistered peppers, salted
Noodles with fresh chili and garlic oil
places.tip: Order the mildest pepper first, since the heat scale counts upward and the cook is watching.

places.name: The Orchard Floor
places.where: the Hollow orchard, by the lake
places.blurb: One table under the Hollow's pear and apple trees, which get their light free from the sunline and their ground dear from the drum. Every course has tree fruit in it, and the last is an apple for every two guests, cut crosswise at the table.
dishes: Pear sliced paper-thin over aged cheese
Cultivated steak, 150 g, with a pear jus
Strawberries under precision cream
The apple, cut crosswise, one for every two guests
places.tip: Watch the cut closely: the cook holds the star up for one breath, and then it is dessert.

places.name: Starch and Salt
places.blurb: Mill cooking the old starch-cuisine way: a big pale staple and a small fierce relish. Papeda-style starch, a fufu-style swallow, farofa-style crumbs toasted in fat, and four relishes in little lidded pots. The relish is the meal.
dishes: Papeda-style starch with a sour yellow broth
Farofa-style crumbs toasted in butter-style fat
Four relishes: chili, sour, green, and the Nine
places.tip: Take more relish than looks polite, as the cook judges guests by the state of the little pots.

places.name: The Swallow
places.blurb: A Mill Hall that serves only its night stew and takes it seriously: three stews a night, each with a stretchy starch swallow pulled to order by a cook who says the pulling is the whole job. Free, and usually full.
dishes: Red palm-style stew with a hand-pulled swallow
Green herb stew, sour and peppery
Mill lager
places.tip: Tear the swallow with one hand and use it as your spoon, the way the regulars do.

places.name: Sugar Glass
places.blurb: A confectioner of the Mill's best work: Karachi-style halwa, lokum, pulled sugar, toffee and sugar glass. Sugar is the cheapest calorie in the drum, and this shop handles it like a precious metal.
dishes: Karachi-style halwa, chewy and bright
Lokum dusted with starch, rose and mint
Sugar glass shattered over cold jelly
Pulled-sugar knot, still warm
places.tip: Watch the sugar being pulled in the window on the hour; the broken knots are given away.

places.name: Twelve Formulas
places.blurb: A Mill-only tasting menu cooked by flavourists: starch, sugar, fat, amino acids and a rack of molecules measured in parts per million. Each course comes with its formula on a card. The plates hold under a kWh of food; the bill is the evening.
dishes: Glycine-proline glaze over warm starch custard
Jasmine aroma three ways, on extruded rice
Sanshool sugar glass that tingles, then goes
Compound chocolate from a cocoa formula in the archive
places.tip: Keep the formula cards: flavourists elsewhere will cook from them, and some will argue with them.

places.name: The Jelly Shop
places.where: the {block} arcade, by the Mill Hall
places.blurb: Cold starch jellies cut and dressed to order: liangfen-style in chili oil and black vinegar, grass jelly in syrup, cubes with garlic and spring onion. A starch jelly is nine-tenths water, so a big bowl costs almost nothing.
dishes: Liangfen-style jelly in chili oil and black vinegar
Grass jelly in black syrup
Jelly cubes with garlic and spring onion
places.tip: Order the big bowl, since a jelly is mostly water and the price barely changes with size.

places.name: The Glass Noodle
places.blurb: Glass noodles cut from the extruder at the counter, served cold in chili oil and black vinegar or hot in a sweet-savoury broth. It is the free table's lunch, done by someone who cares about the cut.
dishes: Cold glass noodles in chili oil and black vinegar
Hot glass noodles in glycine broth with jelly cubes
Lactic sour
places.tip: Ask for the first strands off the extruder, which the cook calls the best of the morning.

places.name: The Nine Bar
places.blurb: The Nine in a dozen versions: pastes, fat-coated sprinkles, a chili oil, a black vinegar, a salted caramel. Each masks the bitterness a different way. Regulars come in for one and leave with a tin.
dishes: Tasting spoon of six Nines
Rice ball with your choice of Nine
The bar's chili oil Nine, by the tin
places.tip: Try the caramel Nine last; it converts people who say the Nine tastes of medicine.

places.name: Almost
places.blurb: A kitchen that makes the Mill imitate dear things, honestly labelled: a sugar-acid tomato that pops, a crackling crust that tastes of steak, an apple made of aroma and jelly. The menu calls each one almost, and is proud of every one.
dishes: Almost tomato: a sugar-acid pearl with a skin
Almost steak: crackling starch with meaty reaction flavour
Almost apple: aroma jelly set in a star mould
places.tip: Order the almost apple last, and cut it yourself, crosswise, as the staff will insist.

places.name: The Puffery
places.blurb: Krupuk-style crackers puffed in hot fat while you wait, in twelve flavours and three sizes, the biggest wider than your face. Crunch comes from oil and sugar here, and this stall has made a living from that for ninety years.
dishes: Big krupuk, wider than your face
Bag of small puffs, chili and lime-style
Sour-starch puffs dusted with the Nine
places.tip: Eat the big one before you board a cab, or its crumbs ride with you to the end of the line.

places.name: Kuih House
places.blurb: Kuih in forty colours and almost as many textures: layered, steamed, chewy and bouncing. Mill starch, sugar, coconut-style cream and a great deal of patience. The lapis is layered all day and cut only at noon.
dishes: Kuih lapis, layered all day, cut at noon
Seri muka, sticky below and green above
Cendol-style jelly in coconut-style cream
places.tip: Come at noon for the cutting; the first slice goes to the oldest person in the queue.

places.name: Last Knotnight
places.where: deck {hdeck}, two corners from the {block} Court
places.blurb: This kitchen cooks the larder its block made at the last Knotnight, crock by crock, through the year. The menu shrinks as the shelves empty, and the last week before Knotnight is rusks and gossip.
dishes: Miso-braised cured mycelium from a numbered crock
Aged cheese with sugar-preserved berries
Hard bread soaked in broth
places.tip: Come early in the year, when the shelves are full and each crock is opened with a speech.

places.name: The Crock Cellar
places.blurb: Pickles from a hundred crocks, lacto-fermented and labelled with the date each was sealed: cucumber, shallot, radish and greens from the racks, and starch jellies soured for a month. Sourness is ranked on a board.
dishes: Pickle plate, six crocks, mild to fierce
Rice with pickle juice and chili crisp
Lactic sour from the oldest crock
places.tip: Ask for the fiercest crock last, with water nearby; the board's top score is earned.

places.name: The Keeping Room
places.blurb: Shelves built to the household rule of ninety days of dry goods, rotated. They cook from the oldest end of the shelf and sell you what keeps from the newest. The most practical dinner in the drum, and better than that sounds.
dishes: Dried noodles in broth, from the oldest tin
Aged cheese and hard rusks
Preserved berry purée with cold custard
places.tip: Buy a tin of the Nine on the way out; it is cheaper here than anywhere, and hosts notice the brand.

places.name: Eleven Days
places.blurb: A menu of what the drum ate in the Eleven Days, cooked by people who were children then: larder food, the Nine, rusks and whatever came by glide from the neighbours. Once a week, for the old and the curious.
dishes: Rusk soup with the Nine, as it was rationed
Cheese from a neighbour's larder, sent by glide
A sugar preserve saved for the eleventh day
places.tip: Ask the cooks where they were on the first day; they will tell you, and that is the reason to come.

places.name: The Pantry Board
places.blurb: A board bar: cheese, cured mycelium, preserves and rusks, with sake and old lager. Everything on the board would survive a long dark, and the staff can tell you for how long.
dishes: The board: two cheeses, cured ham, preserves, rusks
Sake, cold
Larder lager, a year in the cellar
places.tip: Ask how long each thing on the board would keep; the staff answer in days without looking.

places.name: Preserve
places.blurb: Jams and fruit leathers from plant-cell purées, cooked down in vacuum pans on the loop so the colour stays bright. The tea room at the back serves them on sourdough by the spoonful.
dishes: Three jams on sourdough with cultured butter
A strip of berry leather
Black tea
places.tip: Ask for the jam made from real rack strawberries, cooked once a year and sold by the spoon.

places.name: The Tin Shop
places.blurb: A shop of tins: dried noodles, the Nine, preserves, hard cheese in wax. The counter at the back cooks from the tins for anyone who asks. Half the block eats here on nights they spent their wallet on something better.
dishes: Dried noodles from a tin, in broth with the Nine
Wax-rind cheese, a thick slice
Plant-cell plums in syrup
places.tip: Have the Nine on the side, because the cook's tin is older than yours and better.

places.name: Cellar Sours
places.blurb: A cellar of lactic sours, the larder's own drink: pale, tart and kept for years in crocks along the walls. Each crock is dated, and the oldest are poured only at Knotnight. Every glass comes with a bowl of pickles.
dishes: A glass of this year's larder sour
A glass of the five-year sour
The bowl of pickles
places.tip: Order the five-year sour second, once the first glass has taught you what young tastes like.

places.name: Fifty-Five Days
places.where: the Keel, by the oxygen reserve
places.blurb: Named for the air margin a drum has if the beam is cut. The menu is the larder a household would eat through it: dried noodles, aged cheese, miso, preserves, the Nine. Meant as a drill, eaten as comfort.
dishes: Day One bowl: noodles, miso, the Nine
Day Thirty plate: rusks, cheese, preserve
Day Fifty-Five: one sugar sweet, saved
places.tip: Order the Day Fifty-Five sweet even if you are full; the cook keeps a tally of who does.

places.name: The Vintage Table
places.blurb: The drum's blight years cooked as vintages, one a night, from the records: the Neurospora year's orange steak, the yeast year's starch loaves, the year the cultivated fat ran out. The list goes back four hundred years.
dishes: Tonight's vintage: steak from whatever organism that year ate
Blight cheese from the yeast year, griddled
Starch custard, as eaten when the egg line went
Mill lager brewed to that year's recipe
places.tip: Ask for the vintage your hosts' grandparents talk about; with a day's notice the kitchen will cook it.

places.name: Fallback
places.where: Station Ring {ring}, by the Count board
places.blurb: A blight kitchen run by cooks under twenty-five, who learned the menu in the hard years and decided to keep it. Fried starch for chew, coconut-style cheese, the Nine as a seasoning rather than a penance. Full of people from three drums over.
dishes: Crackling starch with chili and black vinegar
Blight-cheese flatbread, griddled until it blisters
Starch custard with black sugar
places.tip: Tell the cooks which dish their parents would never have eaten; they collect the answers on the wall.

places.name: The Orange Year
places.blurb: A steakhouse that serves only Neurospora, the mould the drum switched to when its Fusarium line went down a generation ago. The steaks come out orange, nutty and faintly sweet. People who grew up on them order nothing else.
dishes: Orange mycelium steak with black vinegar butter
Oncom-style cake of the same mould on starch, fried
Frites
places.tip: Order the oncom-style cake with the steak: the same mould grown on starch, and better.

places.name: Mock Fruit
places.blurb: Ten mock fruit pies, each built from crackers, sugar, acids and aroma in a lard-style crust. The apple is the famous one; the pear is better. All began as blight food and are now ordered for birthdays.
dishes: Mock apple pie with cold custard
Mock pear pie, lightly spiced
Mock cherry tart
places.tip: Order the mock pear; the apple is famous for its name, and the cooks know it.

places.name: Library Day
places.where: the Keel, by the strain library doors
places.blurb: When a blighted line comes back from library stock, the drum eats what it missed. This kitchen cooks that day every day: the first steak back, the first real cheese, the first proper loaf, served with a little ceremony.
dishes: The first steak back: mycelium, seared, with butter
First cheese: a young curd, barely aged
First loaf, broken at the table
places.tip: Break the loaf with whoever sits beside you, because the first one is always shared.

places.name: Blight Cheese Bar
places.blurb: Blight cheese, which is coconut-style fat, starch and cheese aroma, done every way the hard years taught: griddled, melted over noodles, fried in cubes. It melts more willingly than the real thing, as the regulars will tell you.
dishes: Blight-cheese toastie, griddled until it blisters
Noodles under melted blight cheese and chili
Fried blight-cheese cubes
places.tip: Start with the fried cubes, which come out of the fat hot enough to need the lid.

places.name: The Lent Table
places.blurb: When the cultivated-fat line goes down, a drum eats without the taste of animals for about forty days. This kitchen cooks that lean stretch all year and makes a case for it: mycelium in koji and garlic, and no fat that ever had a species.
dishes: Mycelium in koji and garlic, no animal fat
Curds in a sesame-style sauce
Steamed greens from the racks
places.tip: Eat the mycelium first, while your tongue still expects the fat and notices it gone.

places.name: Crackling
places.blurb: A commons hall that never stopped cooking its blight menu. When the mycelium went, the cooks fried for chew, and the drum liked it: crackling starch, chili, black vinegar and rice, for nothing. Elders call it the good part of a bad year.
dishes: Crackling starch steak under chili and black vinegar
Sticky rice with the Nine
Mill lager
places.tip: Eat the crackling first, before the vinegar softens it.

places.name: Second Line
places.blurb: A restaurant that cooks with each line's backup organism by choice, so the drum knows what its fallback tastes like before it needs one: a reserve-line steak, a second-culture yoghurt, bread from the reserve gluten. The cook calls it rehearsal.
dishes: Steak from the reserve line, a different chew
Yoghurt from the second culture, sharper
Bread from the reserve gluten, open crumb
places.tip: Ask which line the cook expects to fail next; the answer comes with a shrug and a dessert.

places.name: The Far Table
places.blurb: A kitchen that has cooked from one raft only, six light-years away, for two centuries. It writes back with every menu, and the replies arrive twelve years later. The two kitchens have never met and are old friends.
dishes: Six-year soup, sour and red, from across the Shade
Flatbread from a starter that crossed as a file
Their dessert, as best the cooks can read the measures
Their tea, regrown from a genome
places.tip: Read the newest letter from the other kitchen on the wall; it left their raft when you were about fourteen.

places.name: Arrival Board
places.blurb: A menu like a departures board run backwards: each dish lists the raft it came from, the year the recipe left and the year it arrived. Cooked as written, measures translated, nothing improved.
dishes: Noodles in a broth from a raft three light-years off
A cheese regrown from a file, crumbly and blue
Sweet rice in a syrup nobody here can name
places.tip: Order whatever arrived this month, as the cooks are still learning it and will talk you through every step.

places.name: The Receiving Room
places.where: the Keel, beside the long-letter office
places.blurb: A test kitchen that cooks every recipe the drum receives in its first week, unedited, and serves the results at a long table. About one in five is kept. The rest are filed with notes.
dishes: This week's arrival, whatever it turns out to be
A second try at last week's, corrected
Mill lager, for courage
places.tip: Fill in a card on the dish, since the kitchen reads every one before deciding what to keep.

places.name: Passing Supper
places.blurb: During a Passing, when another raft swings within a few AU, this kitchen cooks its recipes within the hour they arrive and sends a menu back by return. Between Passings it serves the archive. People book for the next Passing years ahead.
dishes: Whatever the passing raft sent this morning
A dish sent to them, which they cooked last week
The archive plate: three dishes from past Passings
places.tip: Between Passings, order the archive plate and ask which dish made the choir cry.

places.name: The Genome Shelf
places.where: the Keel, beside the strain library's receiving bench
places.blurb: The strain library's overflow, with tables: cultures regrown from genomes received by laser, held while the Gate checks them and then, if they behave, eaten. The cheese board has a light-years column.
dishes: Three cheeses from three rafts, with light-years
Bread from a far raft's yeast, a week awake
Koji rice from a line that crossed the Shade
places.tip: Ask the Gate clerk at the corner table which culture failed its checks this week; there is always a story.

places.name: Old Light
places.blurb: Recipes received centuries ago and cooked as written, from rafts that may have changed past recognition since. The cooks treat it as history rather than cuisine, and say so. Some dishes have outlived the kitchens that sent them.
dishes: A soup received six hundred years ago, unchanged
Dumplings from a far archive, folded their way
A sweet whose sender's name is all that is left
places.tip: Read the footnotes, which say what became of each sending kitchen, where anyone knows.

places.name: Reply Kitchen
places.blurb: Every night this kitchen cooks one recipe from a far raft, and the diners vote on which local dish to send back by laser. The replies take years. A board lists the exchanges still waiting for an answer.
dishes: Tonight's far dish, cooked as received
Three local candidates for the reply, small plates
Sake to argue over
places.tip: Vote for the plainest candidate, since the records say far rafts cook the plain ones best.

places.name: Translation
places.blurb: Far recipes with difficult measures: units nobody here uses, ingredients named in words with no match, steps that assume a different gravity. The menu prints each original beside its translation.
dishes: Stew from a raft that spins at half a g, adjusted
Bread rewritten for a different oven
A sweet whose sugar came in an unknown unit, guessed
places.tip: Read the original beside each translation: the cooks' guesses are marked in red and their arguments in the margin.

places.name: The Fortified
places.blurb: Every bottle here is tested for methanol at the bar, with a strip, in front of you: a custom kept from a bad year nobody discusses. The gin is cheap, clean and fortified with thiamine, like the salt.
dishes: House gin over sugar-glass ice
Gin and lactic tonic with a sliver of cucumber
Krupuk and pickles
places.tip: Watch the strip test once, and afterwards you will want it done every time, which is the idea.

places.name: Juniper Cellar
places.blurb: Forty gins, each a formula of a few milligrams of pinene, linalool and citrus esters in Mill spirit. The bar keeps a sprig of real juniper under glass, grown in the racks at absurd expense, and lets you smell it once.
dishes: A flight of three gins, by formula
Gin and soda with garden mint
Salted sour-starch puffs
places.tip: Smell the juniper before your first glass rather than after; the staff say it spoils the gins either way.

places.name: The Licensed Room
places.blurb: This drum taxes spirits hard, and here is where the tax goes: clean gin at four times the cost and a clinic nurse on the stool by the door. Locals grumble at the price. Nobody here has seen a methanol case in years.
dishes: A taxed gin, measured to the drop
A half of fortified lager
Bar snacks with the second glass
places.tip: Pay the tax with good grace; a drum that does not tax spends the difference at its clinic.

places.name: Bitters and Lids
places.where: the {block} Court, under the top terrace
places.blurb: A cocktail cellar where every drink arrives lidded, because heliox carries the aroma off an open glass in minutes. The lid comes off at the table and the room smells of what you ordered. The bartender keeps thirty years of formulas in a tin.
dishes: The house sour, lidded, with a vat egg-white foam
Gin, bitters and black sugar, stirred
Smoke-style old fashioned, lidded until it reaches you
Cheese crisps
places.tip: Lift the lid slowly and keep your face close; the first breath is most of the drink.

places.name: The Sake Cellar
places.where: the cellar under the {block} Mill Hall
places.blurb: Sake brewed from Mill starch and the drum's own koji, in crocks along a wall that holds at 15 °C. Warm, cold or cloudy. The food is pickles and salted curd, which is what sake wants.
dishes: Warm sake in a lidded flask
Cloudy sake, cold
Salted curd and pickles
places.tip: Take the warm flask lidded and pour your own; it is the only warm thing in the cellar.

places.name: The Lager Hall
places.blurb: Mill lager from a brewery behind the bar, pale, clean and cheaper by the pint than a tomato. The hall is loud and the felt is old. The bar food is fried, which costs more than the beer.
dishes: Pint of Mill lager
A plate of fried jelly cubes
Krupuk
places.tip: Order the fried plate early, since the fryer shuts at ten to save the bar's power.

places.name: Sours
places.blurb: Lactic sours and kombucha-style teas for people who want a drink without the gin: sharp, pale and alive, each culture registered with the strain library. Drunk after the baths, in robes, in near silence.
dishes: A glass of the house sour
Kombucha-style tea on garden mint
A dish of salted puffs
places.tip: Come straight from the baths in your robe, as everyone else does.

places.name: Thin Gin
places.blurb: A thin drum's gin cellar: crowded, cheap and cheerful, gin at cost, and bar staff who keep a careful eye on who is drinking which way. The speakers play old recordings that sound spoken through a blanket.
dishes: Gin at cost, with thiamine
Gin and black sugar soda
A bag of krupuk
places.tip: Buy the bar staff a soda rather than a gin, which is the local way to say thanks.

places.name: The Wine Room
places.blurb: Wine fermented in the cellar from plant-cell grape purées, listed by culture rather than place, since there is nowhere for wine to come from. The reds are better than they have any reason to be. The cheese list is short and serious.
dishes: A glass of the house red
A glass of the old white, five years in crock
Cheese and crackers
places.tip: Ask for the culture notes rather than the tasting notes; the sommelier is a strain librarian and lights up.

places.name: The Formula Cellar
places.blurb: A cellar where the drum's flavourists test their spirit formulas on anyone willing: a pear gin with no pear in it, a cocoa spirit, a rice liqueur that tastes of pandan. Samples are free; full glasses are not.
dishes: Pear gin, all aroma and no pear
Cocoa spirit from plant-cell cocoa
Pandan rice liqueur
Salted starch crackers
places.tip: Fill in the tasting card honestly, as the flavourists keep the rude ones and change the formulas.

places.name: Long Strand
places.where: the third-g terrace of the front end wall
places.blurb: Noodles pulled on a terrace at a third of a g, where a hanging strand can stretch three times as long before its own weight tears it. Each bowl is a few long strands rather than many short ones. Slurping is encouraged; the felt is thick.
dishes: Hand-pulled noodles in gelatin-rich broth with koji tare
Long strands, dry, in chili oil
Smacked cucumber with garlic
places.tip: Watch a pull at the window before you order; the third swing is the one to see.

places.name: Night Ramen
places.where: {street}, open from ten until the lamps come up
places.blurb: Ramen in the lamp-night for shift workers and the sleepless: gluten noodles, gelatin-rich broth with koji tare, protein-flour chashu glossed with cultivated pork fat, and a moulded vat egg. Six stools. The bowl stays lidded until it lands.
dishes: Shoyu ramen with chashu and a vat egg
Gyoza-style dumplings, seared on one side
Mill lager
places.tip: Take the end stool by the stockpot, where the cook talks and the second ladle of broth is free.

places.name: Glass and Broth
places.blurb: The Mill Hall's noodle counter, run by a cook who cuts glass noodles by hand when the extruder would do it faster. The broth is the commons' sweet-savoury stock, cooked a little longer than the recipe says. Free, and worth the queue.
dishes: Hand-cut glass noodles in sweet-savoury broth
Jelly cubes fried in the broth's own fat
The Nine, in a pot on the counter
places.tip: Queue at the left hatch for the hand-cut noodles; the right hatch serves the extruded ones.

places.name: Knife-Cut
places.blurb: Noodles shaved straight from a block of gluten dough into the pot, each one thick in the middle and thin at the edges. The cook works at a blur and never looks at the knife. Visitors are asked to stand back.
dishes: Knife-cut noodles in red braise with mycelium
Knife-cut noodles in sour broth with greens
Smacked cucumber
places.tip: Stay behind the line painted on the floor; it was painted after someone stood closer.

places.name: Cold Noodle Bar
places.blurb: Cold noodles in an icy broth of sugar, vinegar and mustard heat, for rooms kept warm against the heliox. The ice is frozen overnight on cheap power, and the bowls sit in it all day.
dishes: Cold buckwheat-style noodles in icy vinegar broth
Cold glass noodles with chili oil and cucumber
Iced barley-style tea
places.tip: Add the mustard a drop at a time; the jar on the counter is stronger than it smells.

places.name: Udon House
places.blurb: Thick gluten noodles trodden underfoot in cloth the old way, then cut and boiled in water drawn hot from the loop. They come in a broth of koji soy and sweet sake, with fried curd on top. The trodden dough is the house pride.
dishes: Udon in koji-soy broth with sweet fried curd
Curry udon with cultivated beef fat
Crisp fritters of starch and garden greens
places.tip: Come at four to watch the dough being trodden; there is a bench, and the cooks treat it as a show.

places.name: The Slurp
places.where: the {block} arcade, under a felt ceiling
places.blurb: In heliox a slurp carries, so noodle rooms hang felt. This one hangs three layers and still sounds like forty people breathing in at once. Plain broth noodles, quick and cheap, for people who eat fast.
dishes: Noodles in broth, the plain bowl
Noodles with chili crisp and the Nine
Lactic sour
places.tip: Slurp: the room is felted for it, and a quiet eater is taken for someone unhappy with the broth.

places.name: Noodle School
places.blurb: The drum's noodle school feeds the public at lunch with whatever the students made that morning, at the cost of the ingredients. The bowls are uneven and the broth is the teacher's.
dishes: Students' hand-pulled noodles in the teacher's broth
Dumplings pleated by the first-years
Smacked cucumber
places.tip: Leave something in the jar by the door, which pays for the students' wander years.

places.name: Laksa Lane
places.where: the {block} night market, under the arcade
places.blurb: Curry noodles in coconut-style cream with chili, sanshool and a sour edge, topped with fried curd and a spoon of sambal-style paste. Rich, cheap and a danger to a mended collar.
dishes: Curry noodles in coconut-style cream with fried curd
Extra sambal-style paste
Iced lime-style soda
places.tip: Wear something already stained and lean in, as the regulars do.

places.name: The Dan Dan Hatch
places.blurb: Dry noodles in sesame-style paste, chili oil and sanshool, under crisped mycelium crumbs. Made in a hatch two metres wide, with one induction ring, one wok and one cook who has done this for forty years.
dishes: Dan dan-style noodles with crisped mycelium
Cucumber in garlic and black vinegar
Sweet soy-style milk
places.tip: Stir from the bottom twenty times before eating, because the sauce sits underneath and the cook counts.

places.name: Rice Sheet
places.blurb: Rice-sheet noodles steamed on cloth in thin layers, rolled round fillings, sliced and drowned in sweet soy. The steamers take loop water up to a boil, so the shop is warm and smells of starch.
dishes: Rice-sheet rolls with mycelium and spring onion
Plain rice-sheet rolls in sweet soy
Jasmine tea
places.tip: Order the plain rolls as well as the filled, since the regulars say the sheet is the dish.

places.name: The Bowl
places.blurb: One bowl, refined over forty years: broth held below a simmer for three days, noodles cut to the millimetre, chashu basted with cultivated pork fat, a vat egg cured in koji. Ten seats. The cook bows when you finish the broth.
dishes: The bowl: three-day broth, koji tare, chashu, cured vat egg
A second nest of noodles, dropped into your broth
Cold barley-style tea
places.tip: Finish the broth: the bow is the cook's whole review of you, and people cross the raft to earn it.

places.name: The Lidded Cup
places.blurb: A tea room where every cup comes with a lid that fits, because in heliox an open cup cools in the time it takes to finish a sentence. Twenty teas, cell-culture and rack-grown, and a plate of rusks.
dishes: Pot of cell-culture black tea, lidded
Jasmine tea from the racks
A plate of rusks
places.tip: Put the lid back between sips, which locals do without thinking and visitors learn by the second cup.

places.name: The Pulled Cup
places.blurb: Milk tea pulled between two jugs at arm's length until it froths, with Mill creamer and black sugar. A cup costs about a tenth of a kWh and comes with a performance. The puller has a following.
dishes: Pulled milk tea
Pulled milk tea with tapioca pearls
Sugar toast
places.tip: Ask for it pulled long; the puller makes a show of it, and the queue does not mind.

places.name: Mended Pots
places.blurb: A tea room on the high decks where the cups are old, the chairs older and the regulars older still. Every teapot has been broken and mended with gold-coloured resin, and the cakes are soft enough for anyone.
dishes: Black tea in a mended pot
Soft sponge with custard
Steamed rice cake
places.tip: Ask who mended your teapot; the name is on the base, and the mender may be at the next table.

places.name: Dusk Tea
places.where: the end-wall terraces, the tier with the best view of the dusk
places.blurb: A tea terrace that opens for the three-hour dusk and closes when the far bank's lamps come on. The tea is ordinary and the cakes are good. The painter's name for the evening is chalked on the board.
dishes: Pot of oolong-style tea
Black sugar cake
Rice crackers
places.tip: Sit facing along the axis, where the dusk runs the whole length of the Hollow towards you.

places.name: Two Leaves and a Bud
places.where: the Keel, beside the tea racks
places.blurb: Tea grown on the drum's own racks, picked as two leaves and a bud, then withered and rolled by hand in the next room. Most tea is cell culture and tastes fine. This tastes of a plant, and the bill is mostly the rolling.
dishes: Rack-grown green tea, first picking
Rack-grown black tea, rolled last month
Sesame-style brittle
places.tip: Ask for the second and third infusions; the leaves are dear, and the staff respect anyone who uses them up.

places.name: The Tea Urn
places.where: the {block} Mill Hall, by the door
places.blurb: The Mill Hall's tea urn, which never goes cold: jasmine tea and milk tea, free all day, with a tray of sour-starch puffs someone always refills. Half the block's arguments start here and most of them end here.
dishes: Jasmine tea from the urn
Milk tea with Mill creamer
Sour-starch puffs from the tray
places.tip: If you take the last puff, refill the tray from the hatch; that is the whole rule.

places.name: Mochi and Tea
places.where: the {block} arcade, by the lift core
places.blurb: Mochi pounded in the window, with matcha-style tea whisked to a froth. A machine does the pounding and a person does the turning, and the turner has all ten fingers and means to keep them.
dishes: Fresh mochi with black sugar syrup
Mochi stuffed with sweet curd
Whisked matcha-style tea
places.tip: Eat the mochi within ten minutes of the pounding; after that it is merely very good.

places.name: Slow Tea
places.where: a clearing among the yews of the {drum} wood
places.blurb: A tea house in the wood where tea is made and drunk in silence. The only instruction, on a slate by the door, says SIT. A pot takes an hour, and nobody looks at the time.
dishes: A pot of rack-grown green tea, slowly
Steamed rice cake, plain
places.tip: Write your thanks on the slate as you leave; the tea master reads them all at lamp-night.

places.name: The Grounds
places.blurb: A coffee room for people who like coffee more than talk. Cell-culture coffee, roasted each morning in an induction drum and ground to order. The spent grounds go down to the Keel to grow mushrooms.
dishes: Cup of cell-culture coffee
Coffee with steamed milk
Butter biscuit
places.tip: Tip your grounds into the bin by the door; the mushroom growers collect at noon, and they check.

places.name: The Rival Pot
places.where: Station Ring {ring}, on the glide platform
places.blurb: A platform tea room serving two blends: the drum's own, and {nb}'s, which comes over by glide each morning. A chalk tally by the door records which one people choose. It has been close for ninety years.
dishes: Our blend, milky and strong
The {nb} blend, which locals call perfume
Rusks for dunking
places.tip: Order both and add your mark to the tally, because the staff take the vote seriously.

places.name: {block} Night Market
places.blurb: A thin drum's night market, which is to say the best cheap food in the drum, cooked on night power while the arcades are fullest. Forty stalls, one long aisle, and everyone shouting over felt that gave up years ago.
dishes: Tapioca crepe with chili crisp and curd
Skewer of seared mycelium
Fried jelly cubes in a paper cone
Lactic soda
places.tip: Walk the whole aisle once before buying anything; the best stall is always the one with no sign.

places.name: The Lamp-Night Fry
places.where: the {block} night market, the far end
places.blurb: A frying stall that opens only in the lamp-night, when the drum's power is cheapest and frying costs least. Puffs, fritters, crisped curds. The stall-holder keeps a chart of the hourly price and fries to it.
dishes: Crisped curds with chili salt
Starch fritters with spring onion
Sour-starch puffs
places.tip: Come at one, when the power price bottoms out and the fryer runs hardest.

places.name: Under the Arcade
places.where: the {street} arcade, after the shops close
places.blurb: When the shops on the arcade shut, their owners wheel out cookers and sell supper from the doorways. A tailor does dumplings, a lamp-mender does noodles, and the grocer does whatever is about to go soft.
dishes: The tailor's dumplings, eight to a plate
The lamp-mender's noodles
The grocer's tomato, sliced, while it lasts
places.tip: Buy from the grocer first, since whatever is about to go soft goes quickly.

places.name: The Queue
places.where: the {block} night market, the corner stall
places.blurb: One stall with a queue that has not been shorter than forty people in living memory. Sticky rice, fried crisp, under a ladle of red braise and pickles. People ride a slow cycler for a week to stand in it.
dishes: Crisp rice under red braise and pickles
A rice ball for the queue
Lactic soda
places.tip: Talk to the people in the queue; it is how regulars pass the hour, and how strangers become regulars.

places.name: The Late Lid
places.where: the {block} night market, under the lift core
places.blurb: A hot pot stall: one pot in the middle of a round table for eight strangers, under a lid only the stall-holder may lift. You drop in what you bought. By the end everyone has eaten some of everyone's.
dishes: A seat at the pot, with broth
Basket of curds, noodles and greens to drop in
Lactic sour
places.tip: Keep to your own quarter of the pot, as a spoon wandering into a stranger's is noticed.

places.name: The Shift Change
places.where: the Keel concourse, at shift change
places.blurb: A market that appears twice a day at the Keel's shift change and is gone within the hour. Everything is hand food: buns, rice balls, skewers, cups of soup. Crews eat walking, which costs food, and buy more.
dishes: Steamed bun with mycelium
Rice ball with a sour plum-style centre
Cup of soup
places.tip: Arrive five minutes before the change and the stalls are yours; one minute after, they belong to the crews.

places.name: Swap Night
places.blurb: A market where most things change hands for other things: jars of pickles, spoons of starter, cuttings from herb shelves, a cake for a mended sleeve. The food stalls take kays, grudgingly.
dishes: Rice cake from the cake swap
A bowl of whatever the soup stall is trading
Herb tea from a swapped cutting
places.tip: Bring a jar of anything: an empty-handed visitor is still fed, but a jar gets you the good soup.

places.name: Skewer Lane
places.blurb: A lane of skewer stalls under a ceiling darkened by generations of glaze. Mycelium, curd, protein-flour sausage and the odd garden pepper, seared on induction rails and brushed with whatever each stall swears by.
dishes: Three mycelium skewers, koji glaze
Protein-flour sausage on a stick
Garden pepper, seared, when there is one
places.tip: Try one skewer from every stall, then buy your second from the best; the stall-holders watch which way you walk back.

places.name: Sweet Lane
places.where: the {block} night market, the sweet end
places.blurb: The end of the market given over to sugar, the cheapest calorie in the drum: pulled toffee, cendol in coconut-style cream, mochi on sticks, sugar glass. Children run the stalls at weekends, one aunt to a stall.
dishes: Pulled toffee on a stick
Cendol-style jelly in coconut-style cream
Mochi on a skewer, toasted
places.tip: Buy from a stall the children run; they give honest change and terrible advice.

places.name: The Free Pot
places.where: the middle of the {block} night market
places.blurb: Among the paid stalls stands a commons pot, kept by the Mill Hall and stirred by whoever is passing: jook in the early night, stew after midnight, free to all. The stall-holders eat from it too.
dishes: Market jook with whatever the stalls gave
Midnight stew with a starch swallow
Chili crisp from the stall opposite
places.tip: Stir the pot once as you pass; the custom is older than the market, and somebody always notices.

places.name: The Star Table
places.blurb: Tables for two, and each table gets one orchard apple, which runs through all eight courses: the star cut crosswise first, the flesh in three dishes, the peel candied, the seeds potted for you to take home. The steak is almost an afterthought.
dishes: The cut: your apple halved crosswise, the star shown
Cultivated steak, 150 g, with apple-peel jus
Apple soufflé on precision casein
Candied peel and a pot of the seeds
places.tip: Plant the seeds you are given: nothing will fruit in a flat, but the seedling is a story for years.

places.name: Twelve Covers
places.where: deck {hdeck}, behind an unmarked door off {street}
