places.blurb: Twelve guests and six cooks, one evening a week. Each cook makes two courses and serves them in person, explaining what each cost and why. The bill is mostly their hours, and the menu prints the arithmetic.
dishes: A course of rack-grown greens, one leaf of each kind
Cultivated steak, 200 g, basted in cultured butter
Black garlic ice cream under spun sugar
A quarter of an orchard pear, cut at the table
places.tip: Read the arithmetic on the back of the menu before dessert, because the cooks ask whether you agree with it.

places.name: The Dim Table
places.where: the heart of the {drum} wood, under the oldest yews
places.blurb: Ten courses served in silence at one table in the dim wood, by hand lamp, with orders and thanks written on slates. Without talk you taste everything. The last course is a single strawberry, and the slates afterwards are mostly about it.
dishes: Jook of Mill jasmine rice, one perfect spoonful
Mycelium held three days on the loop, sliced at the table
Cultivated beef, one thin warm slice
A single rack strawberry
places.tip: Write one line to the cooks on your slate before you leave; it is the only review they read.

places.name: The Wedding Room
places.blurb: Booked mostly for weddings and namings, where the apple is cut crosswise at the table and the star held up for the room. Between weddings it serves the same menu to anyone who asks, and the staff still clap at the cut.
dishes: Cultivated steak, 200 g, basted in cultured butter
Side salad with a cherry tomato each
The apple, one for two, cut crosswise
A glass of the old white
places.tip: Ask to sit near a wedding party if there is one; strangers at weddings are often handed a slice of the star.

places.name: The Shell Egg
places.where: the Keel, behind the henhouse glass
places.blurb: A dozen hens on vat feed behind a glass wall, and a kitchen that cooks nothing but their eggs. Most guests have never seen a yolk sit whole in its white, so the cooks crack each one in front of you.
dishes: One shell egg, fried, on sourdough
Two-egg custard, set on the loop
Yolk cured in koji, grated over rice
places.tip: Order the fried egg rather than the custard, since the custard hides the one thing you came to see.

places.name: Booking Night
places.blurb: A hall room that cooks the Booking Day feast every night, for exactly what a dark day saves: a steak, a salad, half an apple, cheese and wine. Locals come on the anniversaries of good years. Visitors come to see what the fuss is about.
dishes: Cultivated steak, 200 g
Salad with tomato and herbs
Half an orchard apple, cut crosswise
Cheese and a glass of wine
places.tip: Go dark the day before you come; the room seats people wearing the black thread first.

places.name: The Bright Room
places.where: deck {hdeck}, at the bright end of {street}
places.blurb: A dining room lit to a clear noon, a hundred thousand lux, so the food looks the way no lamp-lit kitchen has ever seen it. Light is the dear thing, and the bill charges it by the hour. The staff wear dark glasses.
dishes: Rack salad, shown under full light first
A whole tomato, sliced at the table
Mycelium steak with herb butter
Strawberries and precision cream
places.tip: Look at your hands under the light before you eat; most guests have never seen their own colour at noon.

places.name: The Pear Room
places.where: the {block} Court, on the terrace under the pear wall
places.blurb: A room on the atrium terrace below the block's espaliered pears, which the children pollinate with brushes. When the pears ripen the room serves them, a quarter each, with cheese and wine. Otherwise it serves good food and promises.
dishes: A quarter of a Court pear with aged cheese
Mycelium steak with black garlic butter
Tea of dried pear skin
A glass of the old white
places.tip: Ask when the pears are due; the children who brushed the blossom keep the dates and will tell you.

places.name: The Steak Room
places.blurb: Cultivated steak, 200 g, cut from a slab grown for a month, seared on induction and basted in cultured butter. It costs more than the rest of the menu put together, and the menu is printed so that you notice.
dishes: Cultivated steak, 200 g, basted in cultured butter
Frites and béarnaise
Side salad
Crème caramel
places.tip: Order it rare; the slab grew for a month and the cook takes overcooking personally.
